issues.description: The solution repository provides animal implementations named SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat, while the problem statement and the template (Main.java) clearly expect classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat. Additionally, the solution contains empty files Seal.java, Pig.java, and Goat.java. This naming mismatch between the solution and the specification will confuse students (and automated graders) about the required class names and expected behaviors, and prevents a straightforward comparison between the described UML/classes and the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution repository consistent with the problem statement: provide concrete implementations named Seal, Pig, and Goat (implementing the specified interfaces and extending Animal) or clearly document that the intended classes are SpaceSeal/SpacePig/SpaceGoat and update the problem/template accordingly. Remove or populate the empty Seal.java, Pig.java, and Goat.java files so names and APIs match the specification and template.

issues.description: The template's Farm.java defines a private helper method singFarmSongVerse with its Animal parameter commented out (signature currently has no parameter: private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/)). The UML and the solution expect singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). The commented-out parameter in the template creates a mismatch between the intended method signature and the provided stub, which may confuse students implementing Farm.singFarmSong() and prevent them from calling the helper with an Animal argument without modifying the existing method signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Restore the intended private helper signature in the template: change the method declaration to private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) and update the method body placeholders accordingly. This aligns the template with the UML and the reference solution and avoids forcing students to alter an existing stub to follow the specification.

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to the concrete animal classes as 'Seal', 'Pig', and 'Goat', but the solution repository implements these animals with different identifiers ('SpaceSeal', 'SpacePig', 'SpaceGoat'). This naming mismatch makes it hard for students to directly map the required classes from the exercise description and template to the reference implementation (and to example outputs that use the animal type). It also propagates into the returned messages (e.g. "SpaceGoat <name> is milked") which differ from the expected type names in the problem, increasing cognitive load and confusion.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution identifiers with the problem and template by renaming the reference classes from SpaceSeal/SpacePig/SpaceGoat to Seal/Pig/Goat (or add thin wrapper classes with the expected names delegating to the existing implementations). Also ensure messageOnMilk() and messageOnRide() outputs use the same animal type names expected by the exercise (e.g., use getClass().getSimpleName() or remove the 'Space' prefix in the returned strings).
